title: Toward End-to-End Bearing Fault Diagnosis for Industrial Scenarios with Spiking Neural Networks

problem.claim: Bearing fault diagnosis must bridge high-performance AI methods and real-world industrial scenarios while addressing the constraints of spiking neural networks.

gap.claim: Existing SNN fault-diagnosis methods have inadequate encoding capacity requiring cumbersome preprocessing and non-spike-oriented architectures that constrain performance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Multi-scale Residual Attention SNN (MRA-SNN) for efficient, performant, and robust bearing fault diagnosis.
A multi-scale attention encoding module extracts multiscale fault features from vibration signals and encodes them as spatio-temporal spikes without complicated preprocessing.
Spike residual attention blocks and attention-enhanced spiking neurons are used to improve sparse-spike expressiveness and simulate biological dendritic filtering.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on MFPT, JNU, Bearing, and Gearbox benchmark datasets reportedly show that MRA-SNN significantly outperforms existing methods in accuracy and energy-related performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper applies low-power spiking neural networks to bearing fault diagnosis in industrial scenarios.
It identifies limited encoding capacity and non-spike-oriented architectures as key limitations of existing SNN methods.
It introduces MRA-SNN with multi-scale attention encoding, spike residual attention, and attention within spiking neurons.
It reports extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets with superior results over existing methods.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method combines signal encoding, feature extraction, and neuron-level attention in an end-to-end SNN pipeline.

interpretation.claim: Addressing representation limitations at multiple stages may reduce preprocessing while improving the usefulness of sparse neural signals.

application.claim: For industrial time-series diagnosis, jointly designing input encoding and spike-oriented feature processing may be a useful development strategy.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported benchmark datasets or industrial conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide numerical accuracy or energy results.
The compared existing methods and experimental settings are unspecified.
The supplied evidence does not describe deployment conditions or generalization beyond the listed datasets.
